explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-as-Judge against human judgments on a curated subset of 200 question-answer pairs from NQ-Open dataset, reporting comparative performance metrics and discussing alignment

prompts.notes: Full LLM-as-Judge prompt template provided in Listing 3 with correctness classification examples

guidelines.notes: Used standardized guidelines from referenced work, classifying responses as correct, incorrect, or refuse (refuse treated as incorrect)

sample_size.notes: 200 question-answer pairs from Mistral answers on NQ-Open dataset, curated to include cases where ROUGE and LLM-as-Judge provided conflicting assessments

quantitative_scores.notes: ROUGE showed high recall but alarmingly low precision, while LLM-as-Judge achieved significantly higher precision

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-as-Judge aligns more closely with human assessments than ROUGE, showing significantly higher precision in identifying factual errors while ROUGE exhibits alarmingly low precision despite high recall.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM-as-Judge and human evaluation focus on factual correctness, with LLM-as-Judge additionally assessing semantic equivalence
